methods.label: Choose the blue and yellow positions
methods.explanation:
Number the houses \(1,2,3,4\) in the order Ralph passes them. Since blue comes before yellow and they are not adjacent, there must be at least one position between them.

If blue is first, yellow can be third or fourth. If blue is second, yellow must be fourth. Blue cannot be third or fourth because there would be no later nonadjacent position for yellow. Thus the complete list of blue-yellow position pairs is
\[
(1,3),\qquad(1,4),\qquad(2,4).
\]
For each pair, the two remaining positions are filled uniquely: orange takes the earlier one and red takes the later one. Every valid arrangement has exactly one of the listed blue-yellow pairs, so none is omitted or counted twice. Hence there are \(\boxed{3}\) orderings, choice \(\mathrm{B}\).
methods.levelReason: A short, exhaustive enumeration of positions handles all restrictions without factorial or permutation formulas.
